correctness.rationale: For the two-patch matrix M_m D_i with common mixing m∈(0,1) and strictly ordered growth ratios a_i/b_i, all permutations reduce by cyclic/reversal trace symmetry to three dihedral orders. Product determinants equal (1−2m)^4∏a_i b_i and Perron root is strictly increasing with trace at fixed determinant. Independently expanded exact SymPy polynomial trace differences, obtaining m²(1−2m) times Δ14Δ23, −Δ12Δ34 and −Δ13Δ24, each two-Δ product positive for sorted ratios. Thus 1243>1234>1324 when m<1/2 and reversed when m>1/2, with equality at rank-one m=1/2. All ≤3 seasons are dihedrally equivalent. The given exact rational example yields characteristic polynomial at 1 of positive 641568143/12800000000 for 1243, versus negative −539411857/12800000000 and −13825436857/12800000000, and common determinant <1, so same profiles switch between growth and decline.
residual_risks: No extension proved to unequal seasonal mixing matrices, 3+ patches, random environments or density dependence.
Trace determinant monotonicity applies to positive 2×2 products only; the stated rank-one boundary m=1/2 needs separate handling.
